Article 43

1. Every Child who is a victim of physical and/or psychological Violence as referred to in Article 36 letter g shall receive rehabilitation services both physical and psychosocial.
2. The form of protection for Children who are victims of acts of Violence shall be in the form of basic social services, education, religious guidance, health services, psychological counseling and/or psychotherapy, legal assistance, recreational and educational activities and empowerment of parents of Children who are victims of acts of violence.
3. Every person and/or any party is prohibited from committing acts of Violence against Children.

Article 12

The Regional Government provides Women Protection in the form of:
a. prevention of Violence against Women;
b. provision of services for Women victims of Violence that require coordination at the Regional level; andc. strengthening and developing institutions providing Women Protection services.

REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES OF TANAH BUMBU REGENCY

REGENT OF TANAH BUMBU

DECIDES:

REGIONAL

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION. CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tanah Bumbu Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government organizer who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Head of Region hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Tanah Bumbu Regency. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the people's representative institution of Tanah Bumbu Regency Region. 5. Agency is the Regional Apparatus that organizes government affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection. 6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in organizing government affairs that are the authority of the Region. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that Women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 8. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into men and Women. 9. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a Woman. 10. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a Child who is still in the womb. 11. Child in conflict with the law (ABH) is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child who is a victim of a criminal act and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 12. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 13. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting Women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from Violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security. 16. Toddler is a Child aged 0 (zero) to 5 (five) years, in the early stages of human development. 17. School-Age Child is a Child aged 6 (six) to 18 (eighteen) years. 18. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs for mental and religious guidance as well as clothing, food, shelter, health, education, physical, and social services are not properly fulfilled. 19. Child who is a victim of an act of Violence is a Child who experiences mistreatment such as being abused, humiliated, which endangers the Child physically, mentally and socially. 20. Child maltreatment is all forms of violence against children committed by those who should be responsible and/or those who have power over the child, who should be trusted, namely parents, close family, teachers, supervisors, law enforcement officers, caregivers and companions (World Health Organization). 21. Child in emergency situations is a Child who is in situations and conditions that endanger him/herself such as a Child victim of riots, a Child who is a refugee, a Child victim of natural disasters and a Child in armed conflict. 22. Child in conflict with the law is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child victim of a criminal act, and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 23. Child of isolated indigenous community is a Child who lives in a situation of isolation where they cannot access basic needs. 24. Economically exploited Child is a Child who is forced and/or deceived to be employed by parents or others without being paid or being paid. 25. Sexually exploited Child is the use of a Child for sexual purposes with cash or other forms of compensation between the Child, the buyer of sexual services, intermediaries or agents and other parties who profit from the sexual trade of the Child. 26. Child who is a victim of substance abuse is a Child who suffers from dependence on substances caused by substance abuse, either by their own will or because of encouragement or coercion by others. 27. Child with special needs is a Child who experiences physical and/or mental disabilities that interfere with growth and development in accordance with the stages of Child development. 28. Child victim of maltreatment is a Child who receives treatment that is not in accordance with the rights of the Child. 29. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries that has the authority to regulate and manage Government affairs, the interests of the local Community, based on Community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 30. Child in need of Special Protection is a Child in emergency situations, a Child in conflict with the law, a Child from isolated indigenous communities, a Child who is economically and/or sexually exploited, a Child victim of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other active substance abuse (Napza), a Child victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, a Child victim of physical and/or psychological Violence, a Child with special needs, and a Child victim of maltreatment and neglect. 31.

CHAPTER VII SAFE HOUSE

Article 46

1. Women and Children who are victims of Violence who require ongoing handling have the right to stay in a safe house.
2. The safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall provide a temporary safe place or shelter for victims of Violence until their rights are restored. (3) The operation and management of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus that performs functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
4. Further provisions regarding the operation of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 45

1. Special Protection for Children who are victims of mistreatment and neglect as referred to in Article 36 letter i shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment and rehabilitation.
2. Every person and/or any party is prohibited from placing, allowing, involving, ordering the involvement of Children in situations of mistreatment and neglect as referred to in paragraph (1).

a. ensuring the Child is accompanied by legal counsel; and b. facilitating assistance to Child victims of violence, both in the examination process at court hearings and outside court hearings.
1. Social reintegration

Part Eight

Article 25

1. Rescue actions as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter b are carried out if based on identification results it is known that the Child's safety is threatened.
2. Actions as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by removing the Child from threatening situations and environments.

(3) The SKPD responsible for Child Protection affairs must carry out rescue actions and coordinate with Police Officers/Civil Service Police Units.

Article 41

1. Special Protection for Children who are victims of narcotics abuse including aromatic glue and the like that can cause hallucinogenic effects and the like as referred to in Article 36 letter e, and involved in the use, production and distribution thereof, shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation efforts by the Regional Government and the Community.
2. Every person and/or any party is prohibited from deliberately placing, allowing, involving, ordering the involvement of Children in the abuse, production and distribution of narcotics, aromatic glue and the like as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 42

1. Special Protection for Children who are victims of kidnapping, sale and trafficking as referred to in Article 36 letter f shall be carried out through supervision, protection, prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and reintegration efforts by the Regional Government and the Community.
2. To implement prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government together with the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Courts, Community, NGOs and Social Organizations shall take steps in the form of:a. conducting socialization and/or campaigns on the prevention, handling and elimination of Child Trafficking practices;
b. conducting cooperation with other Regions as well as with other countries through bilateral or multilateral cooperation in accordance with the laws and regulations.
3. Protection for Children who are victims of Child Trafficking shall be implemented through Shelters and/or other Child Protection Institutions, through referrals from government agencies or the Community.
4. Every Child who is a victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, has the right to obtain treatment and rehabilitation both physical, psychological and reintegration in the family environment and the Community.

Sufficiently clear.

Article 46

Point e What is meant by "benefit" is to provide the widest possible benefit for children and women for the interests of society, nation and state.

Point g What is meant by "the best interests of the Child" is that in all actions concerning Children carried out by the Regional Government, parents/family, and the Community, the best interests of the Child must be the primary consideration.
